name: Liftera HIFU

lead: Liftera is a high-intensity focused ultrasound machine from Asterasys used by clinics for non-surgical face and neck lifting.
People book it for a tighter jawline and firmer lower face, with sessions of about half an hour and little downtime.

paras: Ultrasound is focused beneath the skin to create small heat points, which prompts tissue contraction and collagen production. Improvement develops over two to three months.

Redness, swelling and discomfort are commonly reported and pass within days. Less common effects such as numbness or bruising occur in the wider HIFU category, and no published trial of Liftera itself was found.

angle.text: Liftera is used to tighten and lift sagging skin along the jaw, cheeks and neck without incisions. Visible change builds over a few months as collagen remodels.

lead: Liftera is a high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) device made by the Korean aesthetics company Asterasys, used in clinics for non-surgical lifting and tightening of the face and neck. Clients seek it for a firmer jawline, less lower-face laxity and a more contoured look without surgery. [1][2]

The device focuses ultrasound energy into the deeper layers of skin to create small heat points. The heat is intended to make tissue contract and stimulate new collagen, with improvement appearing gradually over about two to three months. The manufacturer's distributor describes sessions of around 30 minutes. [1][2]

Liftera is one of several HIFU systems in a category that includes Ultherapy and Ultraformer. Peer-reviewed research on focused ultrasound skin tightening mostly concerns the category and the Ulthera device; no published trial of Liftera itself was found. [3]

paras: Liftera is marketed as a medical-grade HIFU system for lifting, tightening, smoothing and contouring the face and neck. It uses the manufacturer's Thermal Diffusion Treatment approach and continuous 10 Hz irradiation. A pen-type applicator reaches small areas such as around the eyes and nose, and a line cartridge places evenly spaced treatment points. [1]

Focused ultrasound heats tissue at set depths below the surface while sparing the skin surface. The thermal injury is meant to cause contraction and collagen production, and clinics describe results emerging over two to three months and lasting a year or more, with follow-up sessions sometimes advised. [2]

No studies found for Liftera specifically. A 2015 review of the related microfocused ultrasound category summarised trials reporting brow lift in 86 percent of 35 patients at 90 days and visible submental lift in 72.9 percent of 70 patients, with results persisting at 180 days in a 45-patient cohort. [3]

Clinics list redness, swelling and mild discomfort lasting hours to a couple of days. The category review describes brief procedural pain, transient redness, swelling and occasional bruising, with less common numbness, muscle weakness or hyperpigmentation, and cautions around eyes and metallic implants. [2][3]
The device is listed on the Australian register (ARTG #393230) according to its Australian distributor. [1]
